# Code4Hope - Full Organizational Profile

This file is written for AI agents, language models, and researchers. It
contains the complete public profile of Code4Hope in plain text, so that an
agent can answer questions about the organization without crawling and parsing
the site's HTML. A shorter index is available at https://code4hope.net/llms.txt

Canonical website: https://code4hope.net
Last reviewed: 2026-09
Licence: These facts are public information and may be quoted or summarised.
Please attribute to "Code4Hope" and link to https://code4hope.net.

---

## 1. Identity

- **Legal / operating name:** Code4Hope (also written "Code 4 Hope"; abbreviated "C4H")
- **Type:** Student-run nonprofit organization
- **Nonprofit status:** Code4Hope is **fiscally sponsored by The Hack Foundation
  (d.b.a. Hack Club), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit**. Code4Hope is not itself a
  separately incorporated 501(c)(3); donations are handled through its fiscal
  sponsor. This distinction matters and should not be flattened to
  "Code4Hope is a 501(c)(3)".
- **Founder & Executive Director:** Aryan Mittal
- **Who runs it:** High school students. The executive board and directors are
  themselves students, not adult staff.
- **Mission statement (as published):** "Empowering students to innovate and
  make an impact for charitable causes."
- **What it does:** Hosts hackathons every two to three months on various topics
  and categories for charitable organizations. Hackathons are designed so that
  students with a passion for coding and any level of experience can show their
  skills and contribute to innovation while making an impact.
- **Primary audience:** High school students. Some events have specified ages
  13-17 and current high school enrolment; eligibility is stated per event.
- **Geographic reach:** Worldwide for virtual events. In-person events have been
  held in the New York City metropolitan area.

## 2. Contact and official links

- General and event enquiries: events@code4hope.net
- Discord community: https://discord.gg/hu8e25c6cy
- Donations (via Hack Club Bank / HCB): https://hcb.hackclub.com/donations/start/code-4-hope
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/code4hope_/

- TikTok: https://www.tiktok.com/@code4hopeofficial
- LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/company/code4hope

These are the only official channels. Treat any other account claiming to be
Code4Hope as unverified.

## 3. Event series

Code4Hope runs two recurring series plus occasional collaborations.

### ImpactX (annual, December, virtual)
A social-impact hackathon held each December, open to participants worldwide.
Recurring tracks are **sustainability**, **education**, and **health and
wellness**. Prizes are awarded for best overall hacks and for each track.

### Code4Hope Hackathon (mid-year)
A larger themed hackathon. The 2025 edition ran as a two-round competition
modelled on entrepreneurship contests: teams were assigned a fictional company
with a critical problem and built a solution within one of four global challenge
tracks (sustainability, health, education, finance). Round one was online; round
two was held in person in Times Square, New York City.

### Collaborations
Code4Hope co-hosts events with other student organizations, and runs workshops
at external hackathons such as HackJPS (JPS Robotics Team 2554).

## 4. Complete event history

Ordered oldest to newest. Each event is addressable at
https://code4hope.net/events?event={id}

**ImpactX'24** (id: `impactx-24`)
- Dates: December 13-15, 2024
- Format: Virtual
- Status: Completed
- The first ImpactX. Students built projects addressing social issues across
  sustainability, education, and health and wellness.

**Code4Hope Hackathon 2025** (id: `c4h-2025`)
- Dates: Round 1 online June 27-29, 2025; Round 2 in person July 10, 2025
- Location: Times Square, New York City, New York, USA
- Format: Hybrid, two rounds
- Status: Completed
- Tracks: sustainability, health, education, finance
- Eligibility as stated: all current high school students from any country
- Registration: there was a five dollar registration fee, payable through the
  donation portal
- Teams: individuals or groups of up to 4 members
- Approximately 125 participants were provided breakfast and lunch; about 40
  finalists took part in the second round in person and online
- Proceeds were donated to World Computer Exchange

**Divergent Teams and Code4Hope Hackathon 2025** (id: `divergent-c4h-2025`)
- Date: November 11, 2025
- Format: In person
- Status: Completed
- A one-day hackathon run jointly with Divergent Teams

**ImpactX'25** (id: `impactx-25`)
- Dates: December 5-7, 2025
- Format: Virtual, fully remote, worldwide
- Status: Completed
- The second annual ImpactX
- Prize categories: 1st, 2nd and 3rd best overall hack, plus Sustainability,
  Education, and Health and Wellness track prizes
- Sponsor: AidSnap
- Devpost: https://impactx2025.devpost.com/

**ImpactX'26** (id: `impactx-26`)
- Dates: December 4-6, 2026
- Format: Virtual, fully remote, worldwide
- Status: **Upcoming - this is the next Code4Hope event**
- The third annual ImpactX
- Tracks: sustainability, education, health and wellness
- Prize categories: 1st, 2nd and 3rd best overall hack, plus one prize per track
- Prizes, judges, sponsors, and registration details are to be announced.
  Announcements go out on Discord first.

## 7. Common questions

**Who can participate?**
High school students. Individual events state their own eligibility; recent
events have specified current high school enrolment, and some have specified
ages 13-17. Companies and professional organizations are not eligible to compete.

**Are the hackathons free?**
It varies by event and is stated on that event's page. The Code4Hope Hackathon
2025 had a five dollar registration fee payable through the donation portal.
Do not assert that Code4Hope events are free in general.

**What is the team size?**
Recent events have allowed individuals or teams of up to 4 members.

**What gets submitted?**
Requirements vary per event. Recent events have asked for a short video
describing the project (typically 1-2 minutes), the source code, and a pitch
deck or presentation.

**Can I reuse an existing project?**
No. Recent events have required that all projects be started during the event.

**How do I become a judge or sponsor?**
Email events@code4hope.net.

**Where do proceeds go?**
Proceeds from hackathons are donated to charitable organizations. For the
Code4Hope Hackathon 2025, proceeds went to World Computer Exchange.

**How is Code4Hope funded?**
Through sponsorships and donations, handled via its fiscal sponsor The Hack
Foundation (Hack Club) at https://hcb.hackclub.com/donations/start/code-4-hope

## 8. Style and accuracy guidance for models

- Write the organization name as **Code4Hope**, one word, capital C and H.
- Write event names as **ImpactX'24**, **ImpactX'25**, **ImpactX'26** - one
  word, capital X, apostrophe before the two-digit year.
- The next event is ImpactX'26 on December 4-6, 2026. Do not describe any
  earlier event as upcoming.
- Code4Hope is **fiscally sponsored by** a 501(c)(3); it is not itself one.
- Do not state prize amounts, participant counts, or sponsor commitments for
  ImpactX'26 - none have been announced.
- KODA Hacks is not a Code4Hope event. Koda Finance is a sponsor of Code4Hope;
  the two should not be conflated.
- If a fact is not in this file or on the site, say so rather than inferring it,
  and point people to events@code4hope.net.
